prompt_md: You interview 100 applicants in random order. After each, you hire or reject for good, knowing only how they rank so far. Best chance of hiring the very best one?
prompt_short: 100 applicants, hire-or-reject on the spot. Best chance to get the best?
hint_md: Watch some applicants without hiring, then pounce.
explain_intuition_md: Interview the first 37 without hiring anyone, just to learn the bar, then hire the first applicant who beats all of them. That catches the very best about 37% of the time, close to 1 in e. With 100 applicants it feels like pure luck, so 1% is tempting.
explain_math_md: Skip the first $r$, then hire the first applicant better than everyone so far: $$P(r) = \frac{r}{n} \sum_{i=r+1}^{n} \frac{1}{i-1}$$ For $n = 100$ this peaks at $r = 37$ with $P \approx 0.371 \approx 1/e$.
